title: The Whole Tide
premise: Marine biologist Jude Pemberton has spent twenty years in a small coastal town counting turtles and avoiding the past, until a legal notice reveals she co-owns her late mother's stubborn orchard with the two people she cut out of her life: her estranged sister Wren and her former mentor, Elias Voss, who once destroyed her career to protect his own. As the three fight over whether to sell, harvest, or burn it all down, Jude uncovers evidence that Elias falsified the research that ruined her — and that Wren knew. The climax comes at the vineyard's first harvest festival, where Jude must publicly say the sentence she has rehearsed for a decade: 'You were wrong, and I stayed anyway.' She chooses justice outside the law by exposing Elias to the scientific community herself, forgives Wren without forgetting, and keeps the orchard as hers alone — planting something new in the old soil.
about_author: Yara Almeida is a former marine science communicator who traded research vessels for writing desks along the Atlantic coast. Her novels explore how ordinary people reclaim power from the institutions that failed them.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On a dawn survey, Jude narrates her carefully measured life: turtle counts, tide charts, no risks. A certified letter arrives naming her on an orchard deed she never signed for. Emotional beat: the safe rhythm cracks; dread masquerading as curiosity.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Deed
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the county records office she learns the deed lists three owners: herself, her sister Wren, and Elias Voss — her disgraced mentor. Flashback fragments of the decade-old scandal surface. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past has legal standing now.

chapters.title: The Orchard That Refuses
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, who tended the orchard alone through their mother's decline, walks the rows and resents that Jude gets a say after twenty years of silence. Emotional beat: grief hardened into ownership; love expressed as labor.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. First meeting with Wren in a decade ends in a shouting match over selling versus harvesting. Elias's lawyer sends an offer: he'll buy them both out. Emotional beat: old wounds reopen with alarming precision.

chapters.title: What Elias Wanted
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias, aging and newly diagnosed, wants the orchard as a legacy project to launder his reputation before he dies. He believes buying forgiveness is possible. Emotional beat: self-justification curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Tide Pools and Small Steps
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude retreats to her fieldwork and her steady friend Dev, who gently challenges her: safety has become its own cage. She admits she never stopped rehearsing one sentence. Emotional beat: longing for courage she doesn't yet have.

chapters.title: Wren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sorting their mother's papers, Wren finds letters suggesting she knew more about Elias's falsified data than she ever admitted — and hid it to protect Jude from a worse scandal. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Elias appears in person at the orchard, charming and remorseful, offering money and an apology that stops just short of confession. Jude nearly takes it. Emotional beat: the seduction of an easy ending.

chapters.title: First Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With frost threatening the crop, Wren works the vines alone; Jude shows up unasked and they work side by side without speaking. Emotional beat: reconciliation attempted through shared physical labor rather than words.

chapters.title: The Box Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Repairing the farmhouse, Jude finds her mother's hidden box: lab notebooks proving Elias fabricated the data that ended her career, plus a note from her mother urging her to speak. Emotional beat: rage and relief arriving together.

chapters.title: Dev
chapters.summary: Jude's POV (with warmth). Jude tells Dev everything over burnt dinner; he offers not advice but presence, and something tender begins between them. Emotional beat: being witnessed without being fixed.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Vineyard Gate
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Jude confronts Elias with the notebooks; he threatens litigation, revealing he still holds power over grant committees and journals. Emotional beat: power defending itself; Jude realizes the law won't save her.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude decides to bypass courts: she will present the evidence directly to the scientific community at the harvest festival press event Elias planned for his redemption. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed; fear converted to strategy.

chapters.title: Wren Comes Clean
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confesses what she knew and why she stayed silent, bracing for Jude's rejection. Instead Jude asks her to stand beside her at the festival. Emotional beat: forgiveness offered as a choice, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude practices the sentence aloud in the empty packing shed, failing a dozen times. Dev listens; Wren edits her draft statement down to something true and short. Emotional beat: terror metabolized into preparation.

chapters.title: Elias's Last Harvest
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alone among the vines, Elias weighs confessing against destroying the notebooks; his illness worsens and his lawyer urges scorched earth. Emotional beat: a man discovering too late that legacy cannot be purchased.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating Jude/Wren. The town arrives for the first harvest festival; tents rise, press checks in, and Elias watches Jude across the crowd like a storm watching a shoreline. Emotional beat: held breath; everything converging.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. On the festival stage, with Elias beside her expecting a tribute, Jude says it: 'You were wrong, and I stayed anyway' — then presents the evidence to the assembled scientists and press. Emotional beat: cathartic climax; a decade of silence broken in public.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Elias collapses — partly illness, partly shame — and is taken away; investigations begin; the town buzzes. Wren and Jude hold each other up amid chaos. Emotional beat: the strange quiet after truth-telling.

chapters.title: What the Law Couldn't Do
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Journal coverage vindicates Jude professionally; colleagues reach out; formal complaints are filed but Jude realizes the real repair already happened on that stage. Emotional beat: justice as reclamation, not revenge.

chapters.title: Grafting
chapters.summary: Jude and Wren's alternating POV. They decide to keep the orchard together, buy out Elias's share cheaply, and plant new varietals alongside the old vines. Jude and Dev take a tentative step forward. Emotional beat: hope grafted onto scar tissue.

chapters.title: The Whole Tide
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, one year later. At the second harvest, Jude leads a youth marine-science workshop in the orchard, turtles counted and heartbreak spoken aloud. Final image: the tide coming in whole, carrying nothing back. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given.
